hints: Integrate the left side and use $\sin^2(2x)=\tfrac12(1-\cos4x)$ on the right.
Apply $y=0$ when $x=0$ to determine the integration constant before isolating $y$.
Substitute $x=\tfrac12$ into the exact relation, then use logarithms to find the requested value of $y$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the left-hand side with respect to $y$:
$$\int \mathrm{e}^{-3y}\,\mathrm{d}y = -\dfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{e}^{-3y}$$

Use the trigonometric identity $\cos(4x) = 1 - 2\sin^2(2x) \implies \sin^2(2x) = \dfrac{1}{2}(1 - \cos 4x)$ for the right-hand side:
$$\int \sin^2(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\int (1 - \cos 4x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin 4x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}x - \dfrac{1}{8}\sin 4x + C$$

Apply the initial condition $y = 0$ when $x = 0$ to find the constant $C$:
$$-\dfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{e}^0 = \dfrac{1}{2}(0) - \dfrac{1}{8}\sin(0) + C$$
$$-\dfrac{1}{3}(1) = 0 - 0 + C \implies C = -\dfrac{1}{3}$$

Multiply the entire equation by $-3$ to isolate $\mathrm{e}^{-3y}$:
$$\mathrm{e}^{-3y} = 1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x + \dfrac{3}{8}\sin 4x$$

Take the natural logarithm of both sides and solve for $y$:
$$-3y = \ln(0.5909865) \approx -0.525961$$
$$y = -\dfrac{1}{3}(-0.525961) \approx 0.17532 \dots \approx 0.175$$
